children.title: Deep Learning
children.summary: The slide serves as a title page for a presentation or document section on Deep Learning, specifically focusing on Transformer networks. It lists the authors Jan Platoš and Radek Svoboda, the date May 5, 2026, and their affiliation with the Department of Computer Science at VSB - Technical University of Ostrava.

children.title: Transformer network
children.summary: This section introduces the Transformer network, contrasting it with recurrent neural networks by highlighting its ability to perform parallel computation. It explains the core concept of the attention mechanism, which allows the model to focus on relevant parts of an input sequence, inspired by human reading. The section details how each word is projected into Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V) vectors to compute attention weights using a specific formula, resulting in a new context-aware representation for each word.

children.title: Sinusoidal functions are used to provide:
children.path: Deep Learning - Transformer Network.pdf/Root/Transformer network/Sinusoidal functions are used to provide:
children.summary: This section outlines the benefits of using sinusoidal functions for positional encoding in Transformer networks. It highlights that these functions provide a unique yet smoothly varying encoding for each position, allow for interpolation or generalization to longer sequences, and utilize simple mathematical patterns to capture relative distances.

children.title: Alternative: learned positional encodings
children.path: Deep Learning - Transformer Network.pdf/Root/Transformer network/Alternative: learned positional encodings
children.summary: This section describes an alternative to sinusoidal positional encodings known as learned positional encodings. It notes that in this approach, the positional vectors are trainable parameters. While this method offers more flexibility, it is limited to handling sequence lengths that were seen during the training phase.

children.title: Without PE:
children.path: Deep Learning - Transformer Network.pdf/Root/Transformer network/Without PE:
children.summary: The section titled 'Without PE' explains the critical role of positional encoding in Transformer networks. It states that without positional encoding (PE), a model loses the ability to understand word order, treating sentences with the same words but different arrangements as identical.

children.title: Training a Transformer (Seq2Seq model):
children.path: Deep Learning - Transformer Network.pdf/Root/Training a Transformer (Seq2Seq model):
children.summary: The section details the training process for a Transformer Seq2Seq model, specifically focusing on decoder preparation. It explains that teacher forcing is used where the true previous output is fed into the decoder. The target sequence is right-shifted by one position to prevent the model from copying input, with <sos> and <eos> tokens added at the beginning and end respectively. A causal mask ensures the decoder only sees previous positions during each step. Finally, the loss is computed between the decoder output and the original (unshifted) target sequence.

children.title: Inference – autoregressive decoding:
children.path: Deep Learning - Transformer Network.pdf/Root/Inference – autoregressive decoding:
children.summary: The section titled 'Inference – autoregressive decoding' outlines the step-by-step process for generating text with a Transformer model. The procedure involves inputting the full encoder sequence, starting the decoder with a special start-of-sequence token (<sos>), predicting the first output token, and then iteratively appending each new prediction to the decoder's input until an end-of-sequence token (<eos>) is generated. A key characteristic highlighted is that at every step, the decoder has access to its own previously generated outputs as well as the context from the encoder.
